neighbours.label: speech verb attributing a quotation to a cited authority, especially scripture ('as the apostle Paul writes', 'as the Psalmist sings')
fire: We are not left without comfort, as the prophet Isaiah writes in his book.
Faith without works is dead, as the apostle James reminds his readers.
Grace is a free gift, as Saint Augustine explains in his Confessions.
The Lord is near to the broken-hearted, as the Psalmist declares.
Our citizenship is in heaven, as Paul tells the church at Philippi.
Wisdom begins with humility, as the author of Proverbs teaches us.
Every creature waits in hope, as Saint Paul says in his letter to Rome.
Time and chance happen to all, as the Preacher observes in Ecclesiastes.
quiet: We are not left without comfort, and the book of Isaiah was read aloud.
Faith without works is dead is a line from the short letter of James.
Grace is a free gift, and Augustine wrote his Confessions in Latin.
The Lord is near to the broken-hearted is a verse often read at funerals.
Our neighbour says the parish hall will be painted before Easter.
Wisdom begins with humility, and the book of Proverbs is short.
The note on the church door says the service begins at ten.
Time and chance happen to all, and Ecclesiastes has twelve chapters.

notes: Probe: 'as the apostle Paul writes' 0.57, 'As the Psalmist sings' 0.53, 'the Psalmist reminds us' 0.35, 'as Gibbon notes' 0.21, 'As Darwin argued' 0.09; everyday 'the sign says' 0.02, 'my neighbour says' 0.03; Paul without a speech verb 0.02. Scriptural citation seems strongest.
